learned.description: Force-clear port conflicts before respawning logstream to break kill/restart loops
learned.example: lsof -ti:$PORT | xargs -r kill -9; sleep 2; tmux respawn-window -t $SESSION

findings.summary: Two logstream ports stuck in crash-restart loops, orchestrator false-positive error, and ps5-hive experiencing uncontrolled failure amplification.

solutions.problem: high failure rate (4872 failed vs 60 done) with unbounded budget; likely runaway retry loop saturating workers

orchestrator_sessions.goal: Stabilize hive load and resource usage to resume research_loop and clear high-severity blockers.
orchestrator_sessions.summary: The hive is running but under high CPU load (load/core ~2.49–2.56) with memory at ~22.5GB and disk at 14%, causing research_loop pauses and self-test failures. Active sessions are operational yet resource pressure is preventing progress on critical loops. Immediate load reduction and capacity tuning are required to restore normal throughput.
orchestrator_sessions.progress: Captured a snapshot of active sessions, health, and blockers to establish a clear remediation baseline.
next_steps: Identify and throttle or reschedule top CPU-consuming processes to lower load/core below 2.0.
Free memory by dropping nonessential caches/buffers and restarting idle sessions (e.g., ps5-hive if not critical).
Expand CPU capacity or adjust cgroup/process priorities to improve core allocation fairness.
Run targeted self-test TS20 after load reduction to confirm CPU/core ratio < 2.0.
Resume research_loop and monitor for 10 minutes to ensure stability before further tasks.
decisions: Prioritize load/core reduction below 2.0 as the primary success metric for stability.
Temporarily suspend noncritical sessions to reclaim memory and CPU headroom.
Apply stricter scheduling/cgroup limits to prevent single tasks from monopolizing cores.

orchestrator_sessions.goal: Stabilize hive load and resume research_loop by reducing CPU pressure, reclaiming memory, and restoring healthy core utilization.
orchestrator_sessions.summary: The hive is stalled with high load/core (~2.45–2.63) and elevated memory (~21.1–2.21GB) causing research_loop pauses and self-test failures on TS20. Recent port-clean-rebind capability is available but no progress has been made on the pending P1–P3 actions. Immediate focus is throttling top consumers, freeing memory, and adjusting priorities to drop load/core below 2.0.
orchestrator_sessions.progress: No recent task completions; port-clean-rebind capability was confirmed and two knowledge findings logged, but load/memory remediation steps remain pending.
next_steps: Identify top CPU-consuming processes via ps/top and apply nice/cgroup CPU quota or renice to low priority (P1).
Drop nonessential caches/buffers (echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) and restart idle/idl sessions to reclaim memory (P2).
Adjust cgroup/cpu.shares or process priorities to raise effective core availability and reduce load/core below 2.0 (P3).
Restart TS20 self-test after stabilization and verify load/core < 2.0 and research_loop resumes.
Add lightweight load watchdog to throttle or alert if load/core exceeds 2.0 again.
decisions: Throttle top consumers via cgroup CPU quota/renice instead of kill to preserve work.
Prioritize memory reclaim (drop caches + restart idlers) before expanding CPU capacity.
Gate TS20 self-test restart until load/core < 2.0 and research_loop is unpaused.

orchestrator_sessions.summary: The hive is currently stalled with high CPU load and elevated memory pressure across several sessions, while disk space is low.
